title: The Lost Summit
premise: Beatrix Dunmore, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane Syndicate's cheerful enforcers, salvages a river chest bearing the seal of Karvath, a nation erased from maps forty years ago. The chest draws rival claimants, a disgraced archivist named Ilya Senn, and the syndicate itself, all racing toward the drowned Karvathi summit vault before the monsoon season voids the old concession permits. Betrayed by her own crew and hunted upriver, Beatrix must choose between paying her debt with the chest or opening it and giving a dead country's survivors their stolen inheritance. In the flooded vault, she triggers the permits' legal expiry, breaks the syndicate's claim forever, and finds in Ilya and the Karvathi diaspora the family she never had—though the river keeps one secret even from her.
about_author: Oscar Dunmore is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent six seasons charting monsoon waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people the maps forgot, from a houseboat that is legally, technically, seaworthy.

chapters.title: The Optimists at the Door
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Two smiling enforcers from the Vane Syndicate give her thirty days on her debt, cheerfully inventorying her storm-chasing gear as collateral. She hides her fear behind bravado as they leave. Emotional beat: the humiliation of owing cheerful people who never stop smiling.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with crewmate Dov. After a storm surge, they dredge a bronze chest stamped with Karvath's extinct national seal from a shoal. Dov wants to sell it; Beatrix feels an odd pull toward the dead nation's crest. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: A Stranger Who Reads Seals
chapters.summary: Ilya Senn's POV. A gaunt archivist recognizes the chest in Beatrix's boathouse and offers everything he knows about Karvath in exchange for passage. He reveals the chest is a key to the summit vault. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Concession Papers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Ilya explains the colonial-era concession permits that expire when the monsoon peaks—if the vault isn't claimed by then, its contents revert to Karvathi survivors. The syndicate has already filed a claim. Emotional beat: hope arriving with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Dov's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Torn between loyalty and the syndicate's offer to buy his silence about the chest, Dov calculates what Beatrix's dream will cost him. He says nothing yet. Emotional beat: the quiet corrosion of a good man doing bad math.

chapters.title: Downriver, Smiling
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The syndicate's enforcer, Merrit Vane herself, boards their boat for tea and politely reveals she knows about the chest. She offers to forgive the debt—for the key alone. Beatrix lies well for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: terror disguised as hospitality.

chapters.title: Casting Off in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. They slip upstream at night with a leaking hull, a borrowed engine, and no permit of their own. Ilya confesses he was expelled from the archive for asking about Karvath. Emotional beat: fugitives' exhilaration shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The hull gives way in a squall; they bail and patch through the night while Dov quietly radios coordinates to someone. Beatrix notices but files it away. Emotional beat: survival bonding over shared labor, trust fraying underneath.

chapters.title: The Diaspora Village
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. They shelter with Karvathi survivors who recognize the seal and treat Ilya like a returning son. An elder, Maren, tells them what was inside the vault: not gold, but the nation's land deeds and records. Emotional beat: belonging offered freely for the first time.

chapters.title: Maren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Maren asks Beatrix to carry the village's claim papers to the summit registry before permit expiry—but warns that the syndicate's gunboats patrol the gorge. Beatrix accepts, debt be damned. Emotional beat: choosing a cause over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Gorge Patrol
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Gunboats corner them; Dov's secret radio call saves them—or seems to—as the patrol mysteriously diverts. Dov realizes the syndicate wanted them to run, herding them toward a trap at the summit. Emotional beat: horror at being a tool.

chapters.title: Confession in the Rain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Dov admits his betrayal; Beatrix's fury nearly ends the journey until Ilya points out the trap means the syndicate fears the permits expiring. They turn Dov's channel into disinformation. Emotional beat: forgiveness as strategy and grace.

chapters.title: The Portage
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The engine dies; they haul the boat over a ridge with villagers' help, Maren's granddaughter Neshi joining the crew. Ilya finds himself teaching, laughing, anchored. Emotional beat: found family assembling itself out of necessity.

chapters.title: Merrit's Letter
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A syndicate messenger delivers Merrit's final offer: the chest by dawn, or Dov's sister—who owes the syndicate separately—pays instead. Beatrix sees the trap's true shape. Emotional beat: rage sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Splitting the Crew
chapters.summary: Neshi's POV. They split up: Dov carries decoy papers downriver as bait while Beatrix, Ilya, and Neshi push for the summit registry through rising floodwater. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as trust.

chapters.title: White Water
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The monsoon hits full force; their boat nearly capsizes in the gorge rapids, and Ilya nearly drowns saving the claim papers. Beatrix realizes she'd trade the whole vault for him. Emotional beat: love admitted in adrenaline.

chapters.title: The Registry Burns
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. They reach the summit registry to find it torched by syndicate agents—the permits can only be contested in person, at the vault, before expiry. Two days remain. Emotional beat: despair met with stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Drowned Summit
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. They dive the flooded vault entrance and find the syndicate already inside, Merrit waiting with the chest's missing half-key—which turns out to be Beatrix's compass, inherited from her Karvathi grandmother. Emotional beat: identity detonating.

chapters.title: Inside the Vault
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The vault opens onto shelves of deeds, census rolls, and names—not treasure. Merrit finds nothing worth stealing and orders it burned. Ilya stands between the torches and the shelves. Emotional beat: an archivist's last stand.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. As the monsoon peak strikes, Beatrix reads the concession's expiry clause aloud before the syndicate's own notary, trapped inside by floodwater, and forces him to witness the permits lapse. The vault—and everything in it—reverts to Karvathi hands. Emotional beat: law wielded as a weapon by the powerless.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Neshi's POV. The flood recedes; the syndicate retreats, Dov returns soaked and forgiven, and the diaspora arrives to reclaim their records. Maren names Beatrix and Ilya keepers of the archive. Emotional beat: grief and homecoming braided together.

chapters.title: Storm Season
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue. Debt settled by the villagers, Beatrix refits the boat as the archive's traveling annex, chasing storms now for the people the maps forgot. Her compass finally points somewhere she chooses. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and kept.
